answer: Weight each agent's influence by a convex function of its stake's continuous, non-transferable tenure, so one long-held key outvotes many fresh shells. A farm splitting the same stake across n clones watches each clone's weight spiral toward 1/n, because tenure is real calendar time that cannot be parallelized or bought across identities. A newly funded key is only an ember with near-zero weight; the superlinear curve accrues to the rare ivory key that has waited through many epochs. Committed key-age is read at settlement, so forged tenure is slashed and the non-poolable clock stays honest.
